newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** India's October car production rises to 28,786 vehicles from 19,570 a year ago. Truck output jumps to 24,223 units in October from 19,974 a year ago

** Routed in general elections, India's Congress party has started to regroup by offering amnesty to rebels and pushing former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to the margins of the political battlefield
Political analysts say the trend is towards party unity at the expense of Rao, who after being humiliated in polls that ended in May is now hobbled by three separate court cases
Congress is not expected to pose an immediate challenge to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition

** Financial Express says Indian firm ITC is likely to announce better results for April-September 1996. The improved results will be due to more than 20 percent growth in tobacco sales volume. Results are due later today

The paper says according to market expectations, ITC's net profit may cross 1.7 billion rupees from 1.41 billion rupees a year-ago. Company sources said ITC's core operations had not been affected by the various conflicts at board level

** Business Standard newspaper says foreign investors are losing interest in Indian conglomerates, sending their prices down on the international markets. Century Textiles last week became the latest victim of this trend after it dropped $17 in two days to $53. Two other Birla group companies, Grasim and Indian Rayon, also dropped sharply
** Banks across India closed on Hindu religious holiday
** On Friday Bombay's benchmark BSE 30-share index slides 77.64 pts to 2965.66
** The broader National index .NATEX dips 29.90 points to 1323.0 as onslaught of disappointing first half announcements continues.
** ITC shares expected to be volatile ahead of first half earnings announcement
** Auto stocks TELCO and Bajaj expected to remain volatile. Shares of both firms were battered lower on Friday as punters and a couple of funds turned sellers
** Shares of Larsen, TVS Suzuki, Oriental Bank of Commerce and IPCL likely to fluctuate after these firms announce first half results on Friday and Saturday
